Compare fitted models in sample

Source: R/evaluation.R
compare_models.Rd

The table from evaluate_insample(), plus AICc (GWR), LOOIC (Bayesian GP), convergence and GP-adequacy flags and the residual Moran's I of each fit. No model is refitted. For scores on held-out blocks use compare_models_cv().

Usage

compare_models(fits, newdata = NULL, ...)

Arguments

fits

A spatial_fit, or a named list of them. The names label the rows and must be unique (see evaluate_insample()); a single fit is labelled by its class.

newdata

Optional sf object of held-out rows, carrying the response and the predictors.

...

Passed to predict() when newdata is given. Without newdata nothing reads them, so any argument here is an error, which catches a misspelt newdata.

Value

A data.frame with one row per model and these columns:

model and the metric columns

As in evaluate_insample().

metric_basis

What each row's metrics were computed on (see evaluate_insample). A table that mixes "out-of-bag" and "in-sample" rows does not rank the models, and says so in the log.

AICc (GWR) and LOOIC (Bayesian)

Sums over the rows a model was fitted to, so each column is set to NA, with a warning, when the fits carrying it were fitted to different rows (a predictor with missing values drops rows, for example) or to different responses (a transformed response on the same rows), and the warning says which.

convergence_ok

TRUE or FALSE for a Bayesian fit whose convergence was checked (see fit_bayesian_spatial_model) and NA otherwise. A fit that did not converge is ranked like the others, so it also raises a warning.

gp_adequacy

What the posterior of a Bayesian fit said about its Gaussian-process basis ("ok", "below_resolution", "unresolved_short_range", "no_signal_above_floor" or "not_checked"; see "What the basis resolves" in fit_bayesian_spatial_model) and NA for the other backends. A basis found too coarse scores like one that was adequate, so read the column beside the metrics.

resid_morans_I, resid_morans_z, resid_morans_p

Moran's I of the residuals, from residual_morans_i().

resid_morans_null

The null each model was scored against, since that choice is per fit and governs how much the p-value is worth.

resid_morans_basis

Which residuals the statistic was computed on: always those of the rows the model was fitted to, also when newdata is given, so the column reads "in-sample", or "out-of-bag" for a forest, and never "newdata". Beside metric_basis = "newdata" the Moran columns describe the training residuals, not the prediction errors on newdata, and the two can differ in sign.

A significant p-value is noted in the log (not raised as an R warning): positive autocorrelation as structure the model may have missed, negative (resid_morans_z < 0) as the alternating residuals of a model that tracks its data closely. Read the caveats in residual_morans_i() before treating silence as evidence of no residual structure.

Details

The metrics are those of model_metrics(): see its sections "What the metrics are computed on" and "Percentage errors on responses with zeros".

See also

Other in-sample checks: evaluate_insample(), model_metrics(), print.morans_i(), residual_morans_i()

Examples

library(sf)
set.seed(1)
pts <- st_as_sf(
  data.frame(x = 5e5 + runif(60, 0, 1000), y = 5e6 + runif(60, 0, 1000),
             a = rnorm(60), b = rnorm(60)),
  coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32632
)
# An offset keeps the response away from zero, where MAPE is undefined.
pts$z <- 10 + 2 * pts$a - pts$b + rnorm(60, 0, 0.3)
# Two predictor sets for the same learner: the model that leaves `b` out
# against the one that has it.  These are out-of-bag numbers;
# compare_models_cv() scores the same question on spatial folds.
fits <- list(
  a_only  = fit_rf_model(pts, "z", "a", num_trees = 100, seed = 1),
  a_and_b = fit_rf_model(pts, "z", c("a", "b"), num_trees = 100, seed = 1))
cmp <- compare_models(fits)
cmp[, c("model", "RMSE", "R2", "metric_basis", "resid_morans_I",
        "resid_morans_p")]
#>     model      RMSE        R2 metric_basis resid_morans_I resid_morans_p
#> 1  a_only 1.2209445 0.6804065   out-of-bag    -0.04684408      0.5967265
#> 2 a_and_b 0.7698265 0.8729450   out-of-bag    -0.06447357      0.3977229
